cells.tense: You are practicing the thing that carries meaning onward, and you know you are doing it now.
cells.ask: Invite one person to watch you practice — show the work itself, not the results, and stay while they look.
cells.core:
Whatever this is, you've put the hours in. Some of it you could do with your eyes closed, and that shows up in the room without you saying a word. What's running well is the match: the work and the meaning it carries have become one motion for you.

The work still asks something. Keeping a practice this long also makes it private, and the next person who could carry any of this forward hasn't been let close enough to the making. The unsettled part isn't the practice — it's the door. Ease here looks like leaving it open while you work, so someone can watch the thing being done and not just receive what came out. That's the ask, and it costs you the privacy you built around it.

cells.tense: You are drilling toward a version of this practice that will finally be finished, and it is not coming.
cells.ask: Stop refining before the next session — use whatever's unfinished in front of one other person and let them see it rough.
cells.core:
You're practicing for a future where this is ready. There's one more layer to sand, one more piece of the transmission to get right before it goes anywhere, and the practice has quietly become the place the meaning goes to wait.

What you mean to hand over keeps getting pushed to a later draft. Repetition can hold meaning, but past a point it just holds it still, and the meaning stops traveling. What would genuine showing look like — rough, in front of a person, this week? The practice doesn't need to be ready for that. It needs to leave your hands while it's still imperfect, which is when anything passed on actually moves.

cells.tense: You have set this practice down, and you are still standing at that door.
cells.ask: Do the smallest version of this once this week — ten minutes, no goal — and stop when the time is up.
cells.core:
When this works, it's small and unglamorous: the same action repeated, kept warm by nothing more than coming back to it. The shape of that still sits with you. What has gone quiet is the coming back — the ground has cooled, and the thing you once did sits at a distance you can see but are not currently near.

Start with ten minutes of the plainest piece of it, once, with nothing riding on the outcome. Not the whole structure — just the smallest part, done this week, on its own. That single repetition is where the doing comes back into the body, and it doesn't require a decision about whether you're someone who does this.

cells.tense: You are continuing this practice in ways you haven't admitted to yourself, and the repetition keeps happening anyway.
cells.ask: After one session this week, say out loud once that this practice — the repetition, the refinement — is yours.
cells.core:
On its good days this is the same small action returned to, refined, and kept lit by the returning. You do that here. You come back to it, you sand it one more time, you pick it up again on the days it isn't easy — and you talk as though the practice runs itself and you just happen to be standing where it is.

Look at the plain fact: the same action, done again. That repetition is what makes everything downstream possible, and saying so isn't a boast. The chair was already warm. The practice was continuing before you named it, and naming it doesn't change the practice; it changes who's holding it.
cells.sheetLine: You're already practicing this. It's yours.
